Widen the code_form() self-check of the flow-mode test (#285)

Close TODOs 261, 262 and 263, residuals accepted when pull request 276
merged. tools/test-check-flow-mode.py changes, and this message is
added as .github/squash/285.txt. The check is unchanged, so CODE_SHA256
keeps its value.

TODO 261: some variants of code_form() that strip or rewrite more than
the check's docstrings and the sha256 values of PARAGRAPHS passed the
registry case, because no row tried the condition that they relax.
FORM_PAIRS gains 12 pairs: a string first in the body of a for, a
while, a with and a try; bytes, an assignment of a string and a return
of a string, each first in a function; a string after the docstring of
a function; 2 keyword arguments of a call swapped; and a sha256 in a
list bound to PARAGRAPHS_OLD, in a list bound to PARAGRAPHS by an
annotated assignment and in a list bound to an attribute named
PARAGRAPHS. The last 2 try isinstance(node, ast.Assign) in code_form()
and isinstance(node, ast.Name) in is_name(). MUTATIONS gains 3 rows on
the check's own text: a comparison operator changed, the name __name__
changed and the upper bound of a slice changed.

TODO 262: the 2 MUTATIONS rows that edited the name or the opening
text of a row of PARAGRAPHS tried only the name of its first row and
the opening text of its second. 37 rows built from NAMED replace them.
Each of its 7 rows gets 5: a full stop put at the end of its name, a
full stop put at the end of its opening text, a space put at the end
of its opening text, the first space inside its opening text doubled,
and that space deleted. Each of the 2 opening texts that end with a
space gets 1 more row that deletes that space. For the opening text of
the cycle steps that row makes the same replacement as the removed
opening-text row, byte for byte, under a new label, so it keeps the
coverage of main and adds no catch. Of those 2 rows, only the one for
the opening text of the CODEX ROLE LIMIT is a new edit.

TODO 263: the squash message of pull request 276 says that every edit
of the check's code fails the test until CODE_SHA256 is updated. Only
an edit that changes the check's syntax tree, once its docstrings and
the sha256 values of PARAGRAPHS are left out and the tree is unparsed,
does. Unparsing leaves out the line and column positions that the tree
holds, so an edit that leaves the unparsed tree as it is keeps the
digest. An edit of a comment, of layout, of the quotes of a string, of
how a number is written or of parentheses that change no grouping can
leave that tree as it is, and each of those kinds of edit can also
change it. The edits that change it form a class, of which these are
examples, not a complete list: such an edit can change it inside
the = field of an f-string or inside an interpolation of a template
string; parentheses put around the name that an annotated assignment
targets, or around the targets of a del, can change it; an edit of an
encoding declaration, which is a comment, can change it when a string
in the source is not ASCII; and re-indenting a block that holds a
string written over more than 1 line can change it. The test's module
docstring, the comment on CODE_SHA256 and the docstring of code_form()
now say that unparsing leaves out those positions, that an edit that
leaves the unparsed tree as it is keeps the digest, that an edit of
each of those kinds can leave it as it is and can change it, and that
the edits that change it form a class. The module docstring and the
docstring of code_form() name the examples above as examples, and the
comment on CODE_SHA256 points to the docstring of code_form() for
them. The comment of the registry case says that unparsing leaves out
those positions and that an edit that keeps the unparsed tree keeps
the digest. The docstring of code_form() names the docstrings that it
removes as those of a module, a function, an async function and a
class. PRESERVED gains 3 rows, edits of the check that must keep the
digest: the quotes of a string changed, a number written in
hexadecimal and parentheses that change no grouping added.

Each row is evidence for its own edit only. A code_form() that hides
or keeps only what no row edits still passes, such as one that also
removes a string first in the body of an except clause or of an async
for. An edit of the check that changes its bytes but not that unparsed
tree keeps the digest, by design. The digest's value depends on how
the Python that runs the test unparses a syntax tree; .python-version
names 3.14.4.
